facts_and_myths.claim: Authentic Texas competition chili ('a bowl of red') strictly forbids the inclusion of beans.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Official rules of the International Chili Cookoff sanction disqualification for adding beans; authentic Texas chili contains only meat, peppers, and gravy.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: The 'Chili Queens' of San Antonio operated legendary outdoor night stands serving fiery chili in the 1880s.

facts_and_myths.claim: Chili powder was invented by ancient Aztec cooks.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Commercial blended chili powder was invented in 1894 by German-Texan entrepreneur William Gebhardt to make chili seasoning convenient year-round.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Cincinnati chili is flavored with unexpected sweet spices like cinnamon, cloves, allspice, and unsweetened chocolate.

name: Buffalo Wings
visual_anchor: Platter of crispy deep-fried unbreaded chicken wings tossed in glistening fiery orange cayenne-butter glaze, served with celery sticks and blue cheese dip.
core_traits: Deep-fried unbreaded chicken wing sections coated in vinegar-based cayenne pepper hot sauce and melted butter
Invented at the Anchor Bar in Buffalo, New York, in 1964 by Teressa Bellissimo
Separated into drumettes and flats (wingettes)
Standard party food for sporting events, served with celery sticks and blue cheese dressing

facts_and_myths.claim: Buffalo wings are named after the American bison (buffalo).
facts_and_myths.explanation: They are named after their city of origin: Buffalo, New York, where Teressa Bellissimo first tossed fried wings in hot sauce for her son's friends.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Americans eat over 1.4 billion chicken wings during Super Bowl weekend alone.

facts_and_myths.claim: Traditional authentic Buffalo wings are fried completely naked without any flour breading or batter.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Original Buffalo wings are deep-fried directly in hot oil until skin is crispy, then tossed immediately in hot sauce and butter.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: In Buffalo, locals simply call them 'wings' and almost universally prefer blue cheese over ranch dressing.

name: Pot Roast
visual_anchor: Tender braised beef chuck roast pulling apart into succulent shreds, surrounded by braised whole baby carrots, red potatoes, and thick pan gravy.
core_traits: Classic American comfort food made by braising a tough cut of beef in a covered pot
Utilizes marbled cuts like beef chuck roast, brisket, or round
Cooked low and slow for hours with broth, onions, carrots, and potatoes
Collagen breaks down into luscious gelatin, yielding melt-in-the-mouth meat

facts_and_myths.claim: Braising beef at high, rapid boiling speeds cooks it faster while keeping it equally tender.
facts_and_myths.explanation: High heat causes muscle fibers to tightly seize up and squeeze out moisture; gentle low simmering (190-205 degrees F) is necessary for collagen to melt.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Yankee Pot Roast is distinguished by simmering root vegetables directly in the same pot with the roast.

facts_and_myths.claim: Searing the roast in oil before adding liquid seals the juices inside the meat.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Searing does not seal in juices (meat continues losing moisture when heated), but it creates essential savory flavor compounds via the Maillard reaction.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Mississippi Pot Roast became a viral internet sensation using ranch dressing mix, au jus mix, and pepperoncini peppers.

name: Chicken Pot Pie
visual_anchor: Golden-brown puffed pastry crust cut open to reveal bubbling creamy chicken gravy loaded with tender chicken breast, green peas, carrots, and celery.
core_traits: Savory baked pastry pie filled with diced poultry and vegetables in rich veloute gravy
Filling blends shredded chicken, peas, diced carrots, celery, and sweet corn
Enclosed in flaky all-butter pie crust or puff pastry crust
Historic roots traced to ancient Greek and Roman banquets

facts_and_myths.claim: Roman banquets occasionally served pot pies with live birds baked inside that flew out when sliced open.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Imperial Roman and Renaissance feasts designed surprise pies to amaze guests, inspiring the nursery rhyme 'four and twenty blackbirds baked in a pie'.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: In Pennsylvania Dutch country, 'pot pie' (bott boi) is actually a stovetop stew of square flat egg noodles rather than a baked pastry.

facts_and_myths.claim: Chicken pot pie must always have both a bottom crust and a top crust.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Many traditional versions feature only a single flaky top crust baked over a deep casserole dish to avoid a soggy bottom.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Frozen pot pies were introduced by Swanson in 1951, quickly becoming one of America's first mass convenience meals.

name: Fajitas
visual_anchor: Blazing hot cast-iron skillet hissing with sliced marinated flank steak, charred colorful bell pepper ribbons, and caramelized onions, flanked by warm flour tortillas.
core_traits: Celebrated Tex-Mex dish of grilled marinated skirt steak served sizzling in cast-iron
Accompanied by sauteed strips of sweet bell peppers and sweet yellow onions
Assembled tableside in warm flour tortillas with guacamole, sour cream, and pico de gallo
Originated among Mexican vaqueros (cowboys) in South Texas ranchlands

facts_and_myths.claim: The word 'fajita' is derived from the Spanish word 'faja', meaning belt or sash.
facts_and_myths.explanation: It refers to skirt steak, a diaphragm muscle cut that resembles a belt on the steer carcass, which ranchers gave to vaqueros as part of wages.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: German butcher Sonny Falcon set up the first commercial fajita taco stand at a Texas festival in 1969.

facts_and_myths.claim: Fajitas were historically an ancient Aztec dish eaten in Tenochtitlan.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Fajitas are a modern 20th-century Tex-Mex creation born on Texas ranches along the Rio Grande.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: The theatric 'sizzle' in restaurants is often enhanced by squirting sauce onto the cast-iron right before serving.

name: Enchiladas
visual_anchor: Baking dish of rolled corn tortillas filled with shredded chicken, blanketed in glossy spiced red chili sauce, melted cheese, and crema drizzle.
core_traits: Traditional Mexican dish of corn tortillas rolled around savory meat or cheese fillings
Bathed completely in rich spiced chili pepper sauce (red salsa roja, green salsa verde, or mole)
Baked or pan-warmed and topped with cotija or Monterey Jack cheese and Mexican crema
Derives from the Spanish verb 'enchilar', meaning 'to season with chili pepper'

facts_and_myths.claim: The practice of dipping corn tortillas in spicy chili sauce dates back to pre-Columbian Mayan civilization.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Spanish conquistador Bernal Diaz del Castillo documented Mesoamericans eating rolled tortillas soaked in fiery chili sauce and stuffed with fish.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Swiss Enchiladas (Enchiladas Suizas) are covered in creamy green tomatillo sauce and melted cheese, named for Swiss dairy influence.

facts_and_myths.claim: Authentic Mexican enchiladas are traditionally made using large wheat flour tortillas.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Traditional enchiladas use yellow or white corn tortillas lightly flash-fried in oil so they roll without cracking; flour tortillas turn gummy.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Enchiladas can also be layered flat like a casserole (enchiladas montadas) topped with a fried egg.

name: Ceviche
visual_anchor: Glass bowl of fresh sea bass cubes cured in cloudy lime marinade (tiger's milk), tossed with red onion slivers, cilantro, habanero chili, choclo corn, and sweet potato.
core_traits: Peruvian national culinary treasure of fresh raw fish cured in citrus juices
Citric acid in fresh lime juice denatures fish proteins, effectively 'cooking' it without heat
Seasoned with Peruvian aji amarillo chilis, crisp red onions, sea salt, and cilantro
Served with giant Andean choclo corn kernels and boiled sweet potato slices

facts_and_myths.claim: The leftover zesty, citrus-seafood curing marinade is drunk as an invigorating beverage called 'Tiger's Milk'.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Known as 'Leche de Tigre', this spicy, sour marinade is served in shot glasses as an energy-giving tonic and celebrated hangover cure.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Peru declared National Ceviche Day on June 28th and recognizes it as Cultural Heritage.

facts_and_myths.claim: Ceviche should be marinated in lime juice for at least 12 hours in the refrigerator.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Traditional Peruvian ceviche is marinated for only 5 to 15 minutes right before serving; over-marinating turns delicate fish mushy and dry.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: The ancient Moche civilization preserved fish using fermented passionfruit juices before citrus was introduced.

name: Feijoada
visual_anchor: Large earthenware pot of thick, hearty black bean and pork stew, served with fluffy white rice, toasted manioc flour (farofa), collard greens, and orange slices.
core_traits: National dish and ultimate weekend culinary feast of Brazil
Slow-simmered stew of black turtle beans (feijao preto) and varied cuts of salted, smoked pork and beef
Includes smoked sausage, bacon, ribs, carne-seca, and traditional pork trotters and ears
Accompanied by toasted cassava flour (farofa), braised shredded collard greens, and orange slices

facts_and_myths.claim: Sliced fresh oranges are served alongside Feijoada to aid digestion and balance rich pork fats.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Citric acid and enzymes in fresh oranges cut through the heavy richness and gelatinous fat of the slow-cooked meats.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Feijoada is traditionally eaten during long celebratory Saturday family gatherings accompanied by samba music.

facts_and_myths.claim: Feijoada was originally invented by plantation slaves surviving on scraps discarded by Portuguese masters.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Modern culinary historians found that pork offal was prized by European masters; feijoada evolved from ancient Portuguese and Mediterranean bean stew traditions.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Farofa, toasted cassava flour seasoned with butter and bacon, provides indispensable nutty crunch.

name: Rendang
visual_anchor: Caramelized dark-brown tender beef chunks coated in rich toasted coconut flakes and aromatic chili paste, served with steamed white rice on a banana leaf.
core_traits: Celebrated Indonesian meat dish originating from the Minangkabau people of West Sumatra
Beef slow-cooked in coconut milk and a rich paste of lemongrass, galangal, turmeric leaf, and chilis
Simmered until all liquid evaporates and meat fries gently in its own rendered coconut oil
Voted number one in CNN's global poll of the World's 50 Most Delicious Foods

facts_and_myths.claim: Rendang was historically prepared as durable travel food that could last for weeks without refrigeration.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Slowly evaporating all water and frying meat in coconut oil infused with antimicrobial spices preserves rendang safely in tropical climates.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Minangkabau men embarking on ceremonial wanderings (merantau) carried rendang in wrapped containers.

facts_and_myths.claim: Authentic beef rendang should have a thin, soupy gravy like a traditional curry.
facts_and_myths.explanation: A soupy version is called 'gulai'; as it thickens it becomes 'kalio'; true authentic rendang is completely dry and dark caramelized.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Toasted grated coconut ('kerisik') gives rendang its distinctive nutty, slightly gritty coating.

name: Nasi Goreng
visual_anchor: Plate of dark caramel-glazed stir-fried rice topped with a crispy-edged sunny-side-up fried egg, skewered chicken satay, cucumber slices, and prawn crackers.
core_traits: National dish of Indonesia distinguished from other Asian fried rice styles by sweet soy sauce
Stir-fried in a fiery wok with sweet thick soy sauce (kecap manis) and fermented shrimp paste (terasi)
Aromatic base made from pounded shallots, garlic, chilis, and tamarind
Crowned with a runny fried egg and accompanied by crisp krupuk prawn crackers

facts_and_myths.claim: Kecap manis, the thick molasses-like sweet soy sauce, is what gives Nasi Goreng its unique dark caramel color.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Kecap manis is sweetened with palm sugar and spiced with star anise, caramelizing around individual rice grains in the hot wok.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Former US President Barack Obama fond recalled eating Nasi Goreng during his childhood in Jakarta.

facts_and_myths.claim: Nasi Goreng is made exclusively with fresh hot jasmine rice directly from the steamer.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Just like Chinese fried rice, Nasi Goreng requires cold day-old cooked rice to prevent the grains from turning soggy in the wok.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Adding fermented shrimp paste (terasi) imparts profound savory depth of flavor.

name: Satay
visual_anchor: Bamboo skewers of charred turmeric-marinated chicken sizzling over charcoal, served with thick spiced peanut dipping sauce, cucumber cubes, and rice cakes.
core_traits: Beloved Southeast Asian street food originating on the Indonesian island of Java
Seasoned skewered meat grilled over smoking charcoal and coconut husk embers
Marinated with lemongrass, turmeric, coriander, shallots, and sweet soy sauce
Dipped into velvety, spicy-sweet roasted peanut sauce and served with compressed rice cakes (ketupat)

facts_and_myths.claim: Satay was developed in Java by adapting Arab and Indian kebab grilling techniques to local spices.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Arab traders arriving in the 8th and 9th centuries influenced Javanese street cooks to adapt grilled skewered meats using local peanut sauce.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Turmeric in the marinade gives chicken satay its glowing yellow hue.

facts_and_myths.claim: Satay sauce is made by simply melting regular smooth commercial peanut butter with water.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Authentic satay sauce is freshly ground from roasted peanuts, tamarind, chilis, galangal, garlic, palm sugar, and lemongrass.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Indonesia boasts dozens of distinct regional satay styles, including beef, goat, duck, and pork.

name: Laksa
visual_anchor: Piping hot bowl of fragrant orange curry coconut broth swimming with thick rice noodles, jumbo prawns, fried tofu puffs, fish cakes, and fresh laksa leaves.
core_traits: Signature Peranakan (Straits Chinese) spicy noodle soup celebrated across Malaysia and Singapore
Two main styles: rich coconut milk-based Curry Laksa, and sour tamarind fish-based Asam Laksa
Infused with a pounded rempah spice paste of dried chilis, shallots, galangal, and shrimp paste (belacan)
Garnished with Vietnamese coriander (daun kesum or laksa leaf), cockles, and boiled egg

facts_and_myths.claim: Penang Asam Laksa was ranked number 7 on CNN's list of the World's Best Foods in 2020.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Penang's unique variant uses flaked poached mackerel fish and sour tamarind broth, offering an unforgettable tangy punch.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Fried tofu puffs (tau pok) in curry laksa act like edible sponges that absorb flavorful broth.

facts_and_myths.claim: Laksa broth gets its signature flavor from ground European parsley.
facts_and_myths.explanation: The crucial herb is Persicaria odorata, known locally as 'laksa leaf' or Vietnamese mint, possessing a distinct peppery lemon-citrus aroma.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Katong Laksa in Singapore serves noodles pre-cut into small strands so diners eat the whole dish using only a soup spoon.

name: Hainanese Chicken Rice
visual_anchor: Steaming plate of glistening poached tender white chicken slices served over fragrant chicken-fat rice, with spicy red chili sauce, ginger paste, and dark soy.
core_traits: National culinary pride of Singapore, adapted from immigrants from Hainan, China
Whole chicken gently sub-boiled in master stock and plunged into an ice bath to create silky gelatin skin
Rice sauteed in rendered chicken fat and garlic, then cooked in savory chicken bone broth with pandan leaves
Served with a trio of sauces: fiery garlic-chili sauce, minced ginger paste, and thick sweet dark soy

facts_and_myths.claim: Plunging poached chicken immediately into an ice-water bath creates a delicate layer of jelly beneath the skin.
facts_and_myths.explanation: The sudden thermal shock congeals natural collagen broth into a luscious savory gelatin, keeping meat tender and skin silky.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Culinary legend Anthony Bourdain praised Singapore chicken rice, declaring the rice so delicious it could be eaten completely alone.

facts_and_myths.claim: The chicken meat is supposed to be roasted dark brown under a flame broiler.
facts_and_myths.explanation: The traditional gold standard is pristine poached white chicken ('white cut chicken'), though roasted versions also exist.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Pandan leaves tied into knots perfume the rice cooker alongside crushed ginger and shallots.

name: Beef Stroganoff
visual_anchor: Tender strips of pan-seared beef tenderloin smothered in creamy sour cream mushroom sauce, ladled over a bed of buttered wide egg noodles.
core_traits: Celebrated Russian culinary creation dating to mid-19th century aristocratic Saint Petersburg
Strips of tender beef quickly sauteed with sliced mushrooms and onions
Coated in a velvety sauce enriched with Russian sour cream (smetana) and Dijon mustard
Traditionally served with crisp matchstick potato straws in Russia, or over egg noodles internationally

facts_and_myths.claim: Beef Stroganoff was named after the immensely wealthy Russian aristocratic Stroganov family.
facts_and_myths.explanation: French chef Andre Dupont created the dish for Count Pavel Stroganov in Saint Petersburg, combining French pan sauce with Russian smetana.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Elena Molokhovet's landmark 1871 Russian cookbook documented the first official published recipe.

facts_and_myths.claim: Authentic Russian Stroganoff sauce is made with condensed cream of mushroom soup.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Canned soup was an American convenience shortcut in the 1950s; authentic Stroganoff relies on reduced beef stock, smetana sour cream, butter, and mustard.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Flambeeing the pan with cognac or brandy before adding cream imparts luxurious depth.

name: Chicken Kiev
visual_anchor: Crispy golden breadcrumb-crusted chicken breast cut open, releasing a dramatic fountain of melted garlic-herb butter and chopped fresh parsley.
core_traits: Famous Eastern European chicken dish of pounded chicken breast rolled around cold herb butter
Coated in flour, beaten egg, and fine breadcrumbs before being fried or baked
Cutting into the crisp shell releases a dramatic stream of melted fragrant garlic butter
Named after Kyiv, the capital of Ukraine

facts_and_myths.claim: Diners at formal banquets were once given paper instructions on how to pierce Chicken Kiev without splattering butter on their clothes.
facts_and_myths.explanation: The pressurized molten butter inside the hot crispy shell can squirt several feet across the table if poked carelessly with a knife.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Chicken Kiev was the first ready-made frozen meal ever sold by British supermarket Marks and Spencer in 1979.

facts_and_myths.claim: Chicken Kiev is filled with melted mozzarella and cheddar cheese.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Cheese stuffing is a Chicken Cordon Bleu trait; authentic Chicken Kiev is stuffed strictly with compound herb butter (butter, garlic, parsley, and lemon).
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: The bone of the wing is sometimes left attached, fitted with a decorative paper frill ('papillote').

name: Cabbage Rolls
visual_anchor: Baking dish of plump cabbage leaves stuffed with minced pork and rice, braised in a rich sweet-and-sour tomato sauce, dolloped with sour cream.
core_traits: Comfort food staple across Eastern Europe, Central Europe, and the Balkans
Tender blanched cabbage leaves wrapped tightly around seasoned minced meat, rice, and onions
Baked or simmered gently in rich tomato broth, sauerkraut juice, or mushroom sauce
Known as Golabki in Poland, Holubtsi in Ukraine, and Sarma in the Balkans

facts_and_myths.claim: The Polish name 'Golabki' translates literally to 'little pigeons'.
facts_and_myths.explanation: The name reflects how the plump, folded cabbage rolls resemble small roasted resting pigeons on the dining platter.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: In Sweden, a royal cabbage roll dish called 'Kaldolmar' was brought home by King Charles XII from the Ottoman Empire.

facts_and_myths.claim: Raw, stiff cabbage leaves straight from the garden can be rolled without any prep.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Whole cabbage heads must be boiled or frozen and thawed to soften leaves so they become pliable enough to fold without tearing.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Fermented whole cabbage heads are used during winter in the Balkans to create sour Sarma.

name: Fondue
visual_anchor: Ceramic caquelon pot bubbling over an open flame burner with molten Gruyere and Emmental cheese, surrounded by crusty bread cubes on long fondue forks.
core_traits: Communal Swiss national dish of melted cheese served in a shared ceramic pot (caquelon)
Prepared by melting shredded alpine cheeses (Gruyere and Emmental) with dry white wine and kirsch cherry brandy
Stabilized with garlic and a touch of cornstarch to maintain a smooth glossy emulsion
Diners spear crusty bread cubes on long slender forks and swirl them through the bubbling cheese

facts_and_myths.claim: Swiss fondue tradition dictates that anyone who drops their bread into the pot must pay a fun forfeit penalty.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Swiss custom penalizes dropping bread: historically buying a round of wine, singing a song, or kissing the person on their left.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: The crunchy caramelized cheese crust remaining at the bottom of the pot is prized and called 'la religieuse' (the nun).

facts_and_myths.claim: Fondue was originally invented in 1960s American suburban ski lodges.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Swiss alpine farmers made fondue as early as the 17th century to use up hardened cheese wheels and stale bread through frozen winters.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: The Swiss Cheese Union (Schweizer Kaseunion) aggressively marketed fondue in the 1930s to boost national cheese consumption.

name: Raclette
visual_anchor: A wheel of alpine cheese held under a heating grill, molten cheese scraped with a knife onto steamed baby potatoes, gherkin pickles, and cured charcuterie.
core_traits: Centuries-old Swiss culinary tradition centered on melting semi-hard alpine cheese
Wheel of cheese heated until bubbly and scraped directly onto plates ('racler' means to scrape)
Served over boiled new baby potatoes, pickled gherkins (cornichons), and pickled pearl onions
Accompanied by cured meats like dried beef bresaola and prosciutto

facts_and_myths.claim: Alpine cow shepherds originally melted raclette cheese by placing whole wheels next to open campfires.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Valais shepherds placed halves of cheese near campfire embers, scraping the soft roasted surface directly over boiled potatoes.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: The word 'Raclette' refers to both the traditional dish and the specific AOC-protected Swiss cow's milk cheese.

facts_and_myths.claim: Raclette cheese has a very high melting point and requires intense blowtorches to melt.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Raclette is renowned precisely for its exceptional low-temperature melting properties, flowing smoothly without separating into oil.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Tabletop electric raclette grills with individual small melting pans (coupelles) are popular for holiday parties across Europe.

name: Taco
visual_anchor: Pair of warm doubled corn tortillas filled with charred marinated pork al pastor, topped with fresh diced white onion, chopped cilantro, and a lime wedge.
core_traits: Quintessential Mexican street food consisting of a folded hand-sized corn or flour tortilla
Filled with diverse seasoned meats such as carne asada, carnitas, barbacoa, or al pastor
Garnished classically with finely minced white onions, fresh cilantro, and a squeeze of lime
Served with spicy salsa verde (tomatillo) or smoky salsa roja

facts_and_myths.claim: Tacos al Pastor were inspired by Lebanese immigrants who brought vertical spit-roasting to Mexico.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Lebanese immigrants introduced shawarma to Puebla in the 1930s; Mexican cooks adapted it with marinated pork, achiote, and pineapple.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Hard crunchy taco shells with yellow cheese and lettuce were popularized across the US by Taco Bell founder Glen Bell.

facts_and_myths.claim: Authentic Mexican street tacos are traditionally made with hard pre-shaped yellow taco shells.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Traditional Mexican street tacos exclusively use soft, warm, pliable corn tortillas, often doubled up to prevent tearing.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: The word 'taco' originated from 18th-century Mexican silver miners referring to paper powder charges used to blast rock.

name: Burrito
visual_anchor: Jumbo toasted flour tortilla wrap sliced diagonally, revealing tightly packed layers of seasoned carne asada beef, cilantro rice, black beans, guacamole, and salsa.
core_traits: Large wheat flour tortilla tightly wrapped into a sealed cylinder enclosing diverse savory fillings
Filled with spiced meats, Mexican rice, refried or black beans, cheese, and salsa
San Francisco's Mission District developed the massive foil-wrapped Mission burrito
Translates from Spanish literally to 'little donkey'

facts_and_myths.claim: The burrito was named 'little donkey' because a street vendor transported food in rolled wraps on a donkey.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Folk history in Ciudad Juarez credits vendor Juan Mendez with wrapping hot food in giant tortillas to transport on his donkey across the Rio Grande.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: A deep-fried burrito is called a 'chimichanga', said to be accidentally invented in Tucson, Arizona.

facts_and_myths.claim: Burritos were common daily food throughout all of central and southern Mexico since ancient Aztec times.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Wheat flour tortillas are indigenous to northern Mexico; burritos were barely known in southern Mexico until modern international popularity.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Mission burritos are steamed before rolling to make the flour tortilla pliable enough to hold pounds of filling.

name: Quesadilla
visual_anchor: Golden, toasted corn tortilla folded over a generous filling of gooey melted Oaxaca cheese and squash blossoms, sliced into triangles.
core_traits: Heated folded tortilla filled primarily with melted cheese and savory ingredients
Cooked on a flat griddle (comal) until the tortilla is crisp and cheese is bubbling and stringy
Traditional Mexican varieties use stringy melting Oaxaca cheese (quesillo)
Served with guacamole, pico de gallo, and Mexican crema

facts_and_myths.claim: In Mexico City street stalls, ordering a 'quesadilla' does not automatically come with cheese.
facts_and_myths.explanation: In Mexico City, a quesadilla is a folded tortilla filled with meats, mushrooms, or squash blossoms; customers must explicitly ask to add cheese.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Oaxaca cheese is stretched and wound into large balls resembling yarn.

facts_and_myths.claim: The name 'quesadilla' comes from an indigenous Nahuatl word meaning 'folded tortilla'.
facts_and_myths.explanation: The word is pure Spanish, combining 'queso' (cheese) with the diminutive suffix '-adilla'.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Corn tortillas are traditional in central Mexico, while flour tortillas dominate northern Mexico and Tex-Mex dining.

name: Nachos
visual_anchor: Mountain of crisp triangular tortilla chips smothered in melted cheddar cheese, seasoned ground beef, pickled jalapeno slices, black olives, salsa, and sour cream.
core_traits: Popular Tex-Mex snack consisting of crisp corn tortilla chips covered in melted cheese
Invented in 1940 by Ignacio 'Nacho' Anaya in Piedras Negras, Mexico
Loaded versions topped with refried beans, jalapenos, guacamole, pico de gallo, and sour cream
Standard stadium, cinema, and party snack across the globe

facts_and_myths.claim: Nachos were invented on the fly for the wives of US soldiers stationed in Texas.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Ignacio 'Nacho' Anaya improvised the dish for military wives after restaurant hours by frying tortilla triangles, topping with Colby cheese and pickled jalapenos.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Frank Liberto introduced pumpable liquid cheese sauce for concession-stand nachos at Arlington Stadium in 1976.

facts_and_myths.claim: Traditional original nachos had over twenty complex toppings including rice and barbecue pork.
facts_and_myths.explanation: The original 1940 creation contained only three ingredients: freshly fried corn tortilla chips, melted Wisconsin Colby cheese, and a pickled jalapeno slice.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: The International Festival of the Nacho is held every October in Piedras Negras.

name: Guacamole
visual_anchor: Carved volcanic stone molcajete bowl filled with chunky mashed green avocado dip, speckled with diced red tomatoes, white onions, jalapeno, and fresh cilantro.
core_traits: World-famous Mexican avocado dip dating back to the ancient Aztec empire
Crafted from ripe Hass avocados mashed to a rich, creamy yet chunky consistency
Flavored with fresh lime juice, sea salt, diced onions, cilantro, and minced jalapenos
Traditionally ground tableside using a volcanic stone mortar and pestle (molcajete)

facts_and_myths.claim: Leaving the avocado pit inside the bowl of guacamole prevents it from turning brown.
facts_and_myths.explanation: The pit only protects the avocado flesh directly beneath it from oxygen; browning is caused by the enzyme polyphenol oxidase reacting with air.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Covering guacamole with plastic wrap pressed directly against the surface blocks air and prevents browning.

facts_and_myths.claim: The word 'guacamole' originates from the Aztec Nahuatl language.
facts_and_myths.explanation: It derives from 'ahuacamolli', combining 'ahuacatl' (avocado) and 'molli' (sauce).
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: During Super Bowl Sunday, Americans consume an estimated 100 million pounds of avocados.

name: Salsa
visual_anchor: Rustic glass bowl of vibrant fresh pico de gallo salsa with diced red tomatoes, crisp white onion, diced serrano chilis, fresh cilantro leaves, and lime juice.
core_traits: Ubiquitous Mexican sauce and condiment served alongside chips, tacos, and grilled meats
Varieties range from fresh chunky uncooked relish (pico de gallo) to fire-roasted purees
Built on tomatoes or green tomatillos combined with chilis, onions, cilantro, and lime
Translates from Spanish literally to 'sauce'

facts_and_myths.claim: Salsa surpassed ketchup in annual supermarket retail sales in the United States.
facts_and_myths.explanation: In the early 1990s, the surging popularity of Tex-Mex cuisine pushed salsa past ketchup in US dollar sales volume.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Pico de gallo translates literally to 'rooster's beak', perhaps referencing the bird's pecking motion when scooping it.

facts_and_myths.claim: Green salsa (salsa verde) is made from unripe green red-tomato varieties.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Authentic salsa verde is made from tomatillos (Physalis philadelphica), a tart fruit with a papery husk distinct from regular tomatoes.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Roasting vegetables on a dry griddle before blending produces a deep smoky flavor called 'salsa tatemada'.

name: Shawarma
visual_anchor: Huge rotating vertical spit of stacked marinated meat shavings browning under heating elements, wrapped into thin lavash with garlic toum sauce and pickled turnips.
core_traits: Iconic Middle Eastern street food of seasoned meat roasted on a slowly turning vertical rotisserie
Layers of lamb, chicken, or beef marinated in cumin, cardamom, cinnamon, turmeric, and garlic
Thinly shaved with long knives as the outer layer roasts to a sizzling crust
Wrapped in warm flatbread with garlicky toum paste, tahini, and magenta pickled turnips

facts_and_myths.claim: The word 'shawarma' is an Arabic rendering of the Turkish word 'cevirme', meaning 'turning'.
facts_and_myths.explanation: It directly references the rotation of the vertical spit, which originated in the Ottoman Empire in the 19th century.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: In the 2012 film 'The Avengers', Tony Stark famously invites the superheroes to eat shawarma after saving New York.

facts_and_myths.claim: Shawarma is always served with mayonnaise and tomato ketchup in authentic Middle Eastern stalls.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Authentic chicken shawarma is paired with toum (fluffy emulsified garlic paste), while beef shawarma uses creamy nutty tahini sauce.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Fat from pieces of lamb tail placed on top of the spit renders down continuously, basting the meat stack.

name: Kebab
visual_anchor: Long flat iron skewers of spiced minced lamb kebab sizzling over incandescent lump charcoal, charred with tomatoes and served on flat lavash.
core_traits: Historic culinary family of seasoned meats roasted over open fire across the Middle East and Central Asia
Varieties include skewered meat chunks (shish kebab) and spiced minced meat patties (kofta or seekh)
Seasoned with sumac, onions, cumin, garlic, Aleppo pepper, and fresh parsley
Served over buttery pilaf rice or wrapped in flatbread with grilled peppers and sumac onions

facts_and_myths.claim: Medieval Turkish soldiers are said to have grilled wild game on the blades of their swords over campfires.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Ottoman and Persian military lore attributes the origins of skewered shish kebabs to nomadic soldiers using battle swords over open embers.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Doner kebab served in pita bread with salad and garlic sauce was popularized in 1970s Berlin by Turkish guest workers.

facts_and_myths.claim: The word 'kebab' means 'boiled meat' in ancient Arabic.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Kebab derives from ancient Aramaic and Akkadian roots meaning 'to burn', 'to roast', or 'to char'.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Adana kebab is fiercely protected by geographical designation in Turkey, requiring hand-minced male lamb meat.

name: Falafel
visual_anchor: Deep-fried golden-brown crunchy falafel ball broken open to reveal a vibrant herb-green interior, dusted with toasted sesame seeds beside tahini dip.
core_traits: Deep-fried balls or patties made from soaked ground chickpeas, fava beans, or a combination
Packed with fragrant fresh herbs: flat-leaf parsley, fresh cilantro, garlic, cumin, and coriander
Crunchy, deeply browned exterior with a fluffy, steam-cooked herb-green center
Staple vegetarian street food served inside warm pita with tahini, hummus, and chopped salad

facts_and_myths.claim: In Egypt, authentic traditional falafel (known as ta'ameya) is made exclusively from fava beans.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Egyptian ta'ameya uses soaked split dried fava beans rather than chickpeas, yielding an ultra-creamy, light green interior.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Coptic Christians in ancient Egypt are believed to have created falafel as a hearty meat substitute during Lent.

facts_and_myths.claim: Making falafel requires cooking or boiling the chickpeas before grinding them into paste.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Cooked or canned chickpeas turn into a gummy mush that disintegrates in hot oil; dried chickpeas must only be soaked raw and ground.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Baking soda added just before frying creates a light, airy, and fluffy texture inside.

name: Hummus
visual_anchor: Velvety smooth swirl of pale chickpea hummus in a wide terracotta bowl, pooled with golden extra virgin olive oil, whole chickpeas, and red paprika.
core_traits: Beloved Middle Eastern dip of pureed cooked chickpeas, sesame tahini, lemon juice, and garlic
Smooth, luxurious texture emulsified with cold ice water and olive oil
Served as a cornerstone of the mezze appetizer table with warm pita bread
Translates from Arabic literally to 'chickpea'

facts_and_myths.claim: Peeling the thin translucent skins off boiled chickpeas yields the silkiest, smoothest restaurant hummus.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Removing skins eliminates grainy fiber, allowing blender blades to emulsify the chickpeas with tahini into an ultra-velvety paste.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Lebanon and Israel have repeatedly competed in the Guinness World Records for the largest bowl of hummus ever made.

facts_and_myths.claim: Hummus is naturally an American health food created in modern California.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Recipes for pureed chickpeas with tahini, lemon, and herbs appear in 13th-century medieval Cairo cookbooks.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Baking soda added to chickpea soaking water softens their skins and speeds cooking.

name: Pita Bread
visual_anchor: Round yeast-leavened flatbread puffed into a hollow sphere inside a blazing stone oven, cut open to reveal the interior steam pocket.
core_traits: Ancient round yeast-leavened wheat flatbread originating in the Mediterranean and Middle East
Baked at extreme oven heat (above 370 degrees C / 700 degrees F), causing dough to dramatically puff like a balloon
Steam separates the two layers of dough, creating an internal pocket upon cooling
Used as an edible scoop for dips or stuffed with falafel, shawarma, and gyros

facts_and_myths.claim: Pita bread puffs open into a hollow pocket because water in the dough vaporizes instantly into steam at high heat.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Blistering heat cooks the top and bottom crusts instantly, trapping expanding steam between them to inflate the bread like a balloon.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Flatbread traditions closely related to pita have been baked in the Fertile Crescent for over 10,000 years.

facts_and_myths.claim: All authentic pita bread baked worldwide has a hollow opening pocket.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Greek pita used for gyros is a thicker, pocketless flatbread rolled without puffing so it wraps snugly around meats.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Pita is one of the oldest leavened breads in human gastronomic history.

name: Banh Mi
visual_anchor: Shatteringly crisp, airy golden baguette split and stuffed with savory pork liver pate, cha lua pork roll, pickled daikon and carrot matchsticks, cucumber, fresh cilantro, and red chili.
core_traits: World-celebrated Vietnamese street sandwich harmonizing French colonial and local ingredients
Built inside an ultra-crispy, feather-light baguette made with wheat and rice flour
Layered with rich savory pork pate, mayonnaise, cilantro, cucumber, and spicy chilis
Balanced with crunchy sweet-and-sour pickled daikon radish and carrots (do chua)

facts_and_myths.claim: The baguette used for Banh Mi has a much lighter, crunchier, and airier crust than a traditional French baguette.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Vietnamese bakers incorporate rice flour and proof in humid conditions, creating a paper-thin, crackling crust with a cloud-like crumb.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Oxford English Dictionary officially added the word 'banh mi' to its dictionary in 2011.

facts_and_myths.claim: Banh Mi was originally created in Hanoi during the 18th century.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Banh Mi evolved in Saigon (Ho Chi Minh City) in the late 1950s after French departure, when vendors added local pickled vegetables and meats.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Street carts use custom mini-toasters to recrisp baguettes right before filling.

name: Korean Fried Chicken
visual_anchor: Platter of ultra-crunchy double-fried chicken wings coated in a glistening, sticky red gochujang-garlic glaze, sprinkled with white sesame seeds beside pickled radish cubes.
core_traits: Celebrated Korean street food famous for an ultra-thin, crackling, glass-like crunchy crust
Double-fried in oil to render out all skin fat before being tossed in sticky glazes
Coated in sweet and spicy red chili glaze (yangnyeom) or sweet savory soy-garlic glaze
Central to 'Chimaek' culture: the pairing of fried chicken with cold draft beer

facts_and_myths.claim: Korean fried chicken crust uses potato or cornstarch batter instead of heavy flour to stay crispy for hours.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Potato and cornstarch form a thin, glassy shell that does not absorb moisture, keeping the chicken crispy even when smothered in sauce.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Pickled white daikon radish cubes (chikin-mu) are always served alongside to cut through the grease.

facts_and_myths.claim: Korean fried chicken originated as an ancient royal Joseon Dynasty court banqueting dish.
facts_and_myths.explanation: It evolved in the late 20th century influenced by American military bases and gained national ubiquity during the 1997 financial crisis.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: South Korea has more fried chicken restaurants than McDonald's outlets worldwide.

name: Tteokbokki
visual_anchor: Sizzling wide street cart pan brimming with cylinder rice cakes simmering in fiery crimson gochujang chili broth with sheet fish cakes, scallions, and boiled eggs.
core_traits: Beloved Korean street food snack made of cylindrical chewy rice cakes (garae-tteok)
Simmered in an addictive sweet and spicy sauce of fermented chili paste (gochujang) and chili flakes
Cooked in an anchovy and dried kelp broth alongside fish cakes (eomuk) and hard-boiled eggs
Staple comforting snack sold at pojangmacha tent stalls and school-gate snack bars

facts_and_myths.claim: Historical Joseon royal court tteokbokki was completely non-spicy and seasoned with soy sauce.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Royal Gungjung Tteokbokki featured beef, shiitake mushrooms, and pine nuts simmered in sweet soy sauce centuries before red chilis arrived.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Red spicy tteokbokki was created in 1953 in Seoul by street vendor Ma Bok-lim after accidentally dropping rice cake into black bean sauce.

facts_and_myths.claim: Tteokbokki rice cakes are made by baking wheat dough in bread ovens.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Garae-tteok are made by steaming short-grain white rice flour, pounding it into an elastic dough, and extruding into smooth white cylinders.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Adding instant ramen noodles to tteokbokki creates the immensely popular fusion dish 'Rabokki'.

name: Takoyaki
visual_anchor: Row of piping hot spherical batter balls drizzled in savory brown takoyaki sauce, Japanese mayonnaise, green seaweed powder, and dancing bonito flakes.
core_traits: Iconic Osaka street food of spherical batter dumplings filled with tender octopus chunks
Cooked in custom cast-iron pans with half-sphere indentations and flipped with metal picks
Batter flavored with savory dashi broth, pickled red ginger (beni shoga), and tempura scraps
Garnished with dancing dried bonito flakes (katsuobushi), aonori, and tangy brown sauce

facts_and_myths.claim: The paper-thin bonito fish flakes on top of takoyaki move and 'dance' on their own due to rising steam.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Heat and steam rising from freshly cooked takoyaki cause delicate dried shaved tuna flakes to rehydrate and curl, creating an illusion of dancing.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Takoyaki was invented in Osaka in 1935 by street vendor Tomekichi Endo.

facts_and_myths.claim: Takoyaki balls should be eaten in one giant gulp the second they are removed from the pan.
facts_and_myths.explanation: The molten interior holds extreme steam heat; biting into them immediately can burn the mouth, requiring careful piercing first.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Osaka households commonly own specialized electric takoyaki pans for home family parties.

name: Okonomiyaki
visual_anchor: Thick sizzling cabbage pancake grilling on a steel teppan griddle, latticed with sweet brown sauce and Kewpie mayo, crowned with dancing bonito flakes.
core_traits: Savory Japanese teppanyaki pancake made with shredded cabbage, wheat flour, and grated mountain yam
Name combines 'okonomi' (how you like it / what you want) with 'yaki' (grilled)
Packed with diverse ingredients: pork belly slices, squid, shrimp, and scallions
Two major regional traditions: Osaka style (mixed together) and Hiroshima style (layered with yakisoba noodles)

facts_and_myths.claim: Hiroshima-style okonomiyaki includes a layer of fried yakisoba noodles and a fried egg.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Unlike Osaka style where everything is mixed into batter, Hiroshima style layers thin crepe, shredded cabbage, pork, noodles, and egg sequentially.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Okonomiyaki grew massively in popularity after WWII when wheat flour was provided as relief aid.

facts_and_myths.claim: Okonomiyaki is a sweet dessert pastry eaten with maple syrup and whipped cream.
facts_and_myths.explanation: It is a thoroughly savory, hearty main dish loaded with cabbage, seafood, pork, and umami-rich sauces.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Grated mountain yam (nagaimo) is added to the batter to give the pancake an airy, fluffy interior.

name: Baozi
visual_anchor: Steaming bamboo basket revealing snow-white, pillowy soft pleated yeast buns, torn open to show juicy minced pork and scallion filling.
core_traits: Filled yeast-leavened dough buns steamed in circular stacked bamboo steamers
Soft, cloud-like, pillowy white exterior crimped on top into decorative pleats
Savory fillings include seasoned minced pork, beef, cabbage, or sweet red bean paste
Quintessential everyday Chinese breakfast and street snack eaten with soy and vinegar

facts_and_myths.claim: Legend attributes the invention of steamed buns to legendary Three Kingdoms military strategist Zhuge Liang.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Zhuge Liang reportedly devised meat-filled dough buns shaped like human heads to appease river spirits without sacrificing human lives.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Unfilled plain steamed buns are called 'mantou', while filled buns are called 'baozi'.

facts_and_myths.claim: Baozi buns are made by baking dough in high-heat stone pizza ovens.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Baozi must be cooked with gentle moist steam in bamboo steamers, which keeps the dough pure white and pillowy soft.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Shengjian mantou are a popular pan-fried variety from Shanghai with crispy browned bottoms and soup inside.

name: Samosa
visual_anchor: Platter of golden, crispy triangular fried pastries with flaky blistered crusts, cut open to reveal spiced potato and green pea filling with mint chutney.
core_traits: Famous triangular fried or baked pastry popular across South Asia, the Middle East, and Africa
Encased in a flaky, crisp wheat flour pastry dough (maida) enriched with carom seeds (ajwain)
Filled with spiced potatoes, green peas, onions, coriander, and green chilis
Served with tangy sweet tamarind chutney and refreshing mint-cilantro chutney

facts_and_myths.claim: The samosa originated in ancient Persia and Central Asia before spreading to India.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Historical records mention 'sambusak' in 10th-century Middle Eastern texts, carried to medieval Indian royal courts by traveling merchants.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: In Central Asia and the Horn of Africa, meat-filled baked versions are known as 'sambusa'.

facts_and_myths.claim: Traditional Indian samosas were always made with potatoes throughout ancient history.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Potatoes are native to South America and were only introduced to India by the Portuguese in the 16th century; earlier samosas used minced meat.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Carom seeds (ajwain) rubbed into the pastry dough provide a distinctive herbal thyme-like aroma.

name: Naan
visual_anchor: Teardrop-shaped flatbread blistered with smoky dark char marks and brushed with melted garlic butter and chopped cilantro, fresh from a clay tandoor.
core_traits: Leavened, oven-baked flatbread quintessential to South Asian and Central Asian dining
Slapped directly onto the searing hot clay walls of a cylindrical tandoor oven
Dough enriched with yogurt, milk, and yeast to produce an elastic, pillowy, chewy texture
Brushed immediately with melted ghee or butter, minced garlic, and fresh coriander

facts_and_myths.claim: Bakers stretch naan dough into teardrop shapes by slapping it against their forearms before sticking it to oven walls.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Gravity stretches the hanging dough as chefs slap it against the scorching interior clay walls of a tandoor with a cloth pad.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: The word 'naan' derives from the Persian word for bread ('nan').

facts_and_myths.claim: Naan and Roti are two words for the exact same kind of bread.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Roti is unleavened, made from whole wheat flour (atta), and cooked on a flat griddle; naan is leavened, uses white flour (maida), and is baked in a tandoor.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Peshawari naan is a famous sweet variation stuffed with crushed almonds, raisins, and desiccated coconut.

name: Roti Canai
visual_anchor: Golden-brown circular flatbread with flaky crispy outer layers fluffed into airy crinkles by clapping hands, served with a bowl of spicy dhal curry.
core_traits: Malaysian and Singaporean layered flatbread influenced by Indian immigrant traditions
Dough made with ghee, repeatedly twirled and tossed in the air until paper-thin and translucent
Folded into circular coils and griddled on a flat iron tava until puffed and crispy
Clapped vigorously between two hands immediately after cooking to fluff the flaky layers

facts_and_myths.claim: Cooks clap the freshly griddled hot flatbread between their bare hands to separate the internal layers.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Clapping crushes the crisp crust and forces air between the buttered layers, making the flatbread immensely flaky and light.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Roti Canai was ranked the #1 street food in the world by TasteAtlas in 2023.

facts_and_myths.claim: Roti canai is exclusively eaten as an afternoon sweet dessert.
facts_and_myths.explanation: It is predominantly a savory breakfast staple eaten with dhal (lentil curry), mutton curry, or spicy sambal at outdoor mamak stalls.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Skilled mamak chefs twirl the dough like a pizza spinner until it is thin enough to read newspaper print through.

name: Poutine
visual_anchor: Cardboard takeout dish overflowing with crispy brown french fries, squeaky white cheddar cheese curds, and smothered in piping hot savory brown gravy.
core_traits: National comfort food dish of Quebec, Canada, originating in rural dairy regions in the 1950s
Composed of three sacred ingredients: crispy hot french fries, fresh cheese curds, and piping hot gravy
Fresh cheese curds must be squeaky between the teeth and melt slightly without liquefying
Brown gravy (traditionally light chicken and beef reduction) ties the hot dish together

facts_and_myths.claim: Authentic Quebec poutine strictly requires fresh cheese curds that 'squeak' when chewed.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Fresh unpressed cheddar curds have elastic protein strands that create a distinct squeaking sound against tooth enamel.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Legend claims vendor Fernand Lachance exclaimed 'Ca va faire une maudite poutine!' ('That will make a damn mess!').

facts_and_myths.claim: Traditional poutine is made with shredded yellow cheddar cheese melted under a salamander broiler.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Using shredded or melted cheese is rejected by Quebecers; curds must remain warm, soft, and intact from the hot gravy.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Upscale restaurants now serve gourmet poutine topped with duck confit, foie gras, and shaved black truffles.

name: Corn Dog
visual_anchor: Golden-brown, smoothly battered hot dog on a thick wooden stick, drizzled with a zigzag pattern of bright yellow mustard, resting on carnival paper.
core_traits: Beloved American state fair and carnival food on a wooden stick
Sausage or frankfurter skewered and coated in a thick, sweetened cornmeal batter
Deep-fried until the exterior forms a smooth, golden, crunchy sweet crust
Convenient handheld food eaten on the go with mustard or ketchup

facts_and_myths.claim: The Texas State Fair claims credit for popularizing the corn dog nationally via Fletcher's Corny Dogs in 1942.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Brothers Carl and Neil Fletcher introduced fried cornmeal-battered wieners at the State Fair of Texas, turning it into a fairground legend.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: In Australia and New Zealand, a similar battered hot dog on a stick is called a 'Dagwood Dog' or 'Pluto Pup'.

facts_and_myths.claim: Corn dogs are coated exclusively with wheat pancake batter with zero cornmeal.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Authentic corn dogs derive their signature gritty crunch, golden hue, and sweet flavor from stone-ground yellow cornmeal in the batter.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Korean corn dogs have surged globally, featuring hot dogs half-stuffed with mozzarella and rolled in cubed potatoes or sugar.

name: Onion Rings
visual_anchor: Stack of giant golden-brown fried onion rings showing airy, bubbled beer batter crust, served with a ramekin of zesty horseradish dipping sauce.
core_traits: Popular appetizer and side dish made from cross-sectional slices of whole onions
Onion rings dipped in seasoned flour, beer batter, or breadcrumbs and deep-fried
Cooks until the batter is crunchy while the onion inside steams to sweet tenderness
Standard companion to hamburgers, barbecued ribs, and steaks in American diners

facts_and_myths.claim: Sweet onion varieties like Vidalia and Walla Walla are prized for producing the best onion rings.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Their high sugar and low sulfur content allow rings to caramelize into sweet, tender bites without sharp raw pungent bite.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: A recipe for fried onions dipped in batter was published in a London cookbook as early as 1802.

facts_and_myths.claim: Fast food chain onion rings are always sliced directly from whole intact raw onions.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Many commercial chains use diced onion paste extruded into uniform rings so customers do not pull the whole onion out on the first bite.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Dredging onion slices in cornstarch before dipping prevents the batter from slipping off during frying.

name: Mozzarella Sticks
visual_anchor: Golden breaded mozzarella stick pulled in half to reveal a dramatic, stretchy, gooey bridge of melted white cheese beside warm red marinara sauce.
core_traits: Elongated batons of mozzarella cheese coated in seasoned Italian breadcrumbs and deep-fried
Fried quickly so the exterior turns crunchy while the interior turns into gooey, stretchy cheese
Celebrated for the iconic 'cheese pull' when snapped in half
Standard sports bar and diner appetizer served alongside warm marinara dipping sauce

facts_and_myths.claim: Freezing the breaded mozzarella sticks solid before frying prevents the cheese from bursting out into the hot oil.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Deep-frying frozen sticks gives the breadcrumb crust time to brown and crisp without over-expanding and blowing out melted cheese.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: The earliest documented fried cheese recipe appeared in the medieval French cookbook 'Le Menagier de Paris' in 1393.

facts_and_myths.claim: Mozzarella sticks were invented in Naples, Italy, by pizza makers.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Modern breaded finger mozzarella sticks became widespread in the 1970s across American taverns with the arrival of mass deep-fryers.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Double-dredging in flour, egg wash, and breadcrumbs ensures an impenetrable seal for the molten cheese.

name: Pretzel
visual_anchor: Lustrous mahogany-brown twisted Bavarian soft pretzel with cracked surface and coarse white salt crystals, served with sweet mustard and German beer.
core_traits: Traditional baked pastry distinguished by its symmetrical looped knot shape
Dipped in food-grade lye (sodium hydroxide) solution before baking to create deep mahogany color and glossy crust
Pillowy and chewy interior with coarse sea salt crystals sprinkled on top
Cornerstone of Bavarian beer halls and American shopping mall street kiosks

facts_and_myths.claim: Dipping raw dough into a lye bath is the chemical secret behind a Bavarian pretzel's dark mahogany crust.
facts_and_myths.explanation: The extreme alkalinity of lye rapidly accelerates the Maillard reaction in the oven, producing the pretzel's signature color, shine, and flavor.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Christian monks allegedly invented the twisted knot shape to represent arms crossed across the chest in prayer.

facts_and_myths.claim: Hard crunchy pretzels were invented before soft chewy pretzels.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Soft bread pretzels are centuries older; hard crunchy pretzels were born in 19th-century Pennsylvania when a baker accidentally over-baked soft pretzels.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: The pretzel has served as the official guild emblem of European bakers since the 12th century.

name: Bratwurst
visual_anchor: Plump grilled German bratwurst sausage blistered over charcoal embers, split inside a crusty bread roll with spicy brown German mustard and sauerkraut.
core_traits: Traditional German sausage typically made from finely minced pork and veal
Seasoned with marjoram, caraway seeds, nutmeg, and ginger
Pan-fried or grilled over glowing coals until browned and crisp-skinned
Staple of German beer gardens, street kiosks (Imbiss), and American tailgates

facts_and_myths.claim: The oldest documented recipe for Bratwurst dates back to Nuremberg in 1313.
facts_and_myths.explanation: City council records in Nuremberg established strict pork quality regulations for 'Bratwurst' over 700 years ago.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Nuremberg bratwursts are famously finger-sized, served three in a bun ('Drei im Weggla').

facts_and_myths.claim: The prefix 'Brat-' in Bratwurst comes from the German verb 'braten', meaning 'to fry'.
facts_and_myths.explanation: It derives from the Old High German word 'Brato', meaning finely chopped or lean minced meat, though modern German associates it with frying.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Wisconsin is regarded as the Bratwurst capital of the United States.

name: Currywurst
visual_anchor: Sliced grilled pork sausage drenched in warm spiced curried ketchup sauce and heavily dusted with aromatic yellow curry powder on a paper tray with fries.
core_traits: Quintessential post-war Berlin street food fast food dish
Steamed and fried pork sausage sliced into bite-sized bite coins
Smothered in a warm sauce of spiced tomato ketchup and Worcestershire sauce
Generously dusted with aromatic Indian curry powder and served with french fries or bread rolls

facts_and_myths.claim: Currywurst was invented in post-WWII Berlin by a woman trading with British soldiers.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Herta Heuwer obtained ketchup and curry powder from British soldiers in 1949, mixing them with grilled sausage at her street stand.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Germans consume an estimated 800 million currywursts every year.

facts_and_myths.claim: Currywurst sauce is made from traditional Indian coconut curry gravy.
facts_and_myths.explanation: The sauce is fundamentally seasoned tomato ketchup infused with curry powder, paprika, vinegar, and onions.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Berlin operated a dedicated Deutsches Currywurst Museum for a decade.

name: Arepa
visual_anchor: Golden griddled round pre-cooked cornmeal patty split open and stuffed with shredded beef, black beans, fried sweet plantains, and white cheese.
core_traits: Staple round flatbread made of ground pre-cooked maize dough prominent in Colombia and Venezuela
Cooked on a flat griddle (budare) or baked until the exterior forms a crispy toasted crust
Venezuelan style: split open like a pocket and stuffed with meats, avocado, and cheese
Colombian style: often served un-split, topped with butter, melted cheese, or eggs

facts_and_myths.claim: Pre-cooked corn flour (masarepa) was invented in the 1950s to replace hours of manual corn grinding.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Venezuelan engineer Luis Caballero Mejia invented the instant pre-cooked corn flour process, commercialized globally under the Harina P.A.N. brand.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: The 'Reina Pepiada' arepa is stuffed with chicken salad and creamy avocado, named after a Venezuelan beauty queen.

facts_and_myths.claim: Arepas are made from nixtamalized corn flour identical to Mexican corn tortillas.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Arepas use pre-cooked maize flour that is boiled before grinding without wood ash or lime nixtamalization, giving a distinct mild corn flavor.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Indigenous Timoto-Cuica tribes ate arepas long before Spanish colonizers arrived in South America.

name: Empanada
visual_anchor: Baked crescent golden pastry turnover with decorative braided rope edge (repulgue), cracked open to reveal juicy spiced ground beef, green olives, and hard-boiled egg.
core_traits: Baked or fried pastry turnover popular across Latin America, Spain, and the Philippines
Name derives from the Spanish verb 'empanar', meaning to coat or wrap in bread
Wheat or corn dough folded over spiced ground beef, chicken, ham and cheese, or vegetables
Edges sealed with intricate braided pleating patterns (repulgue) that identify fillings

facts_and_myths.claim: Different folding patterns on empanada crusts are used as a visual code for what filling is inside.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Bakers use distinct repulgue edge designs (braided, fork-pressed, scalloped) so customers can tell beef, chicken, or cheese apart without cutting.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Argentina's Tucuman province hosts the National Empanada Festival every September.

facts_and_myths.claim: Empanadas were originally created in Mexico during the 19th century.
facts_and_myths.explanation: The earliest empanadas were documented in 16th-century Galicia, Spain, originating from medieval Catalan cookbooks.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Argentine beef empanadas in Mendoza feature chopped sweet raisins and green olives.

name: Tamale
visual_anchor: Steaming bundle wrapped in dried corn husks tied with a string, unwrapped to reveal moist golden corn masa encasing tender red chili braised pork.
core_traits: Ancient Mesoamerican food made of seasoned nixtamalized corn masa dough
Filled with shredded pork, chicken, salsa, or sweet raisins
Wrapped in dried corn husks or banana leaves and steamed until firm and fragrant
Traced back thousands of years to ancient Maya, Aztec, and Olmec civilizations

facts_and_myths.claim: You are supposed to eat the dried corn husk wrapper along with the steamed tamale inside.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Corn husks are tough, fibrous steaming vessels used solely to hold the masa together and perfume it; they are always unwrapped and discarded.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: In 1976, US President Gerald Ford committed a famous political gaffe by biting directly into a tamale husk at the Alamo.

facts_and_myths.claim: Tamales served as portable, shelf-stable military rations for ancient Aztec and Maya warriors.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Warriors carried steamed tamales wrapped in leaves on military campaigns because they were portable, nutrient-dense, and could be reheated over coals.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: The Spanish singular is 'tamal', while 'tamale' is the anglicized singular.

name: Pupusa
visual_anchor: Thick, griddled corn cake stuffed with bubbling melted quesillo cheese and chicharron, served with tangy pickled cabbage slaw (curtido) and tomato salsa.
core_traits: National dish of El Salvador made of thick, handmade corn or rice dough cakes
Stuffed before cooking with quesillo cheese, refried beans, or seasoned pork paste (chicharron)
Griddled on a flat comal until browned with crispy melted cheese edges oozing out
Traditionally eaten with hands and accompanied by curtido (spiced pickled cabbage relish)

facts_and_myths.claim: El Salvador passed a national law dedicating the second Sunday of November as National Pupusa Day.
facts_and_myths.explanation: The Legislative Assembly declared pupusas the National Dish of El Salvador in 2005 to celebrate cultural heritage.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: A pupusa stuffed with cheese, pork, and beans all together is called 'pupusa revuelta'.

facts_and_myths.claim: Pupusas are cut into pockets and filled after cooking, exactly like Venezuelan arepas.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Pupusas are stuffed raw: dough is indented into a cup, fillings are placed inside, sealed into a ball, and patted flat before hitting the griddle.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Indigenous Pipil tribes made early vegetarian pupusas filled with squash flowers and wild herbs.

name: Churros
visual_anchor: Fluted, ridged golden-brown fried choux pastry batons rolled in cinnamon sugar, served alongside a small cup of thick, bittersweet Spanish dipping chocolate.
core_traits: Traditional fried dough pastry popular across Spain, Portugal, and Latin America
Piped through a star-shaped nozzle (churrera) directly into boiling oil to create deep ridges
Rolled immediately while hot in granulated sugar and fragrant ground cinnamon
In Spain, served for breakfast with an intensely thick, molten drinking chocolate

facts_and_myths.claim: Piping churro dough through a star-shaped nozzle is essential to prevent it from exploding in hot oil.
facts_and_myths.explanation: The ridges formed by the star nozzle allow expanding steam to escape; smooth dough forms a sealed crust that can violently burst.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Spanish shepherds allegedly created churros over campfires because bread was hard to bake in the mountains.

facts_and_myths.claim: Churros in Madrid are always filled with sweet dulce de leche or chocolate cream inside.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Traditional Spanish churros are thin, solid, and unfilled, dipped into hot chocolate; thick filled churros are a Latin American variation.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Thicker, wider Spanish fried dough batons are called 'porras'.

name: Crepe
visual_anchor: Paper-thin, golden lacy French crepe folded into a triangle, drizzled with melted dark chocolate and filled with sliced strawberries and whipped cream.
core_traits: Ultra-thin French pancake originating in the northwestern region of Brittany
Made by spreading thin liquid batter over a circular cast-iron billig griddle using a wooden T-spreader (rozell)
Sweet crepes made with wheat flour, sugar, and milk; savory buckwheat crepes called galettes
Folded into triangles or rolled around diverse fillings like Nutella, bananas, or ham and Gruyere

facts_and_myths.claim: French tradition says holding a gold coin in your left hand while successfully flipping a crepe brings wealth for the year.
facts_and_myths.explanation: On La Chandeleur (Candlemas, Feb 2), families flip crepes with their right hand while holding a gold coin for good fortune.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Crepes Suzette features a sauce of caramelized sugar, butter, orange zest, and Grand Marnier flambeed tableside.

facts_and_myths.claim: Crepe batter should be whipped vigorously and cooked immediately without any resting period.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Crepe batter requires resting for at least 30 to 60 minutes so air bubbles dissipate and gluten relaxes, preventing rubbery pancakes.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Buckwheat galettes from Brittany are historically paired with dry sparkling apple cider.

name: Panini
visual_anchor: Crusty ciabatta bread sandwich pressed on a ribbed contact grill with prominent grill char lines, filled with melting mozzarella, prosciutto, and basil pesto.
core_traits: Italian sandwich made with crusty artisan bread like ciabatta or focaccia
Warmed and flattened in a heavy ribbed electric press or contact grill
Filled with Italian charcuterie (prosciutto, mortadella), cheeses (mozzarella, provolone), and vegetables
Heat melts the cheese inside while creating a shatteringly crispy exterior crust

facts_and_myths.claim: In Italy, ordering 'one panini' is grammatically incorrect.
facts_and_myths.explanation: In Italian, 'panino' is the singular noun for a bread roll or sandwich; 'panini' is the plural form meaning multiple sandwiches.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: During the 1980s in Milan, trendy fashion-conscious youth who congregated in sandwich bars were dubbed 'Paninari'.

facts_and_myths.claim: Traditional Italian panini must always be slathered with American mayonnaise and yellow mustard.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Italian panini rely on extra virgin olive oil, tapenades, or pesto; heavy mayonnaise and sweet yellow mustard are foreign additions.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Ciabatta bread was invented in 1982 by a baker in Verona to counter the French baguette monopoly.

name: Calzone
visual_anchor: Crescent-shaped golden baked dough turnover with blistered crust, cut open to reveal steam and molten ricotta, mozzarella, pepperoni, and fresh basil.
core_traits: Italian oven-baked folded turnover made from salted pizza dough
Originated in 18th-century Naples as a portable, handheld street food version of pizza
Stuffed with ricotta cheese, mozzarella, cured meats like salami or prosciutto, and vegetables
Translates from Italian literally to 'trouser' or 'pant leg'

facts_and_myths.claim: The word 'calzone' literally translates from Italian to 'trouser' or 'stocking'.
facts_and_myths.explanation: It was named because its folded pouch shape resembled the baggy trousers worn by Neapolitan dockworkers.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: In Naples, calzones are often fried in hot oil rather than baked, known as 'pizza fritta'.

facts_and_myths.claim: Authentic Italian calzones are filled with tomato sauce on the inside and covered with more sauce on the outside.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Traditional Neapolitan calzones place cheese and meat inside with little or no sauce to prevent a soggy crust; marinara sauce is served on the side.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: A rolled-up pizza sandwich with sauce inside is called a 'stromboli', an Italian-American invention from Philadelphia.

name: Bruschetta
visual_anchor: Thick slices of grilled rustic sourdough bread rubbed with raw garlic, piled high with diced sweet red tomatoes, fresh basil ribbons, and dark balsamic glaze.
core_traits: Classic Italian antipasto of grilled rustic bread rubbed with raw garlic and drizzled with olive oil
Originated in ancient Rome where olive growers tested the quality of fresh pressed oil on toasted bread
Most famous modern topping: diced vine-ripened tomatoes, fresh torn basil, garlic, and sea salt
Derives from the Roman dialect verb 'bruscare', meaning 'to toast over coals'

facts_and_myths.claim: In proper Italian pronunciation, 'bruschetta' is pronounced with a hard 'sk' sound ('broo-SKET-tah').
facts_and_myths.explanation: In Italian phonetics, 'ch' before 'e' always produces a hard 'k' sound, not the soft 'sh' sound frequently heard in English.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: The bread is vigorously scraped with a peeled clove of raw garlic while still steaming hot from the grill.

facts_and_myths.claim: The word 'bruschetta' refers to the tomato and basil topping rather than the toasted bread.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Bruschetta strictly refers to the grilled, garlic-rubbed bread itself; toppings can be beans, sauteed greens, meats, or nothing at all besides olive oil.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Crostini are smaller, made from thin baguettes, while bruschetta uses thick rustic sourdough slabs.

name: Arancini
visual_anchor: Golden-brown breaded fried rice ball cracked in half, revealing saffron-infused risotto, rich meat ragu center, green peas, and molten stringy mozzarella.
core_traits: Traditional Sicilian street food consisting of stuffed cooked rice balls coated in breadcrumbs and deep-fried
Named 'arancini' (little oranges) because their spherical shape and golden-orange fried color resemble oranges
Typically filled with slow-cooked meat ragu with peas, or ham and mozzarella
Conical shaped in eastern Sicily around Catania to represent Mount Etna, and spherical in Palermo

facts_and_myths.claim: In Catania, arancini are shaped into pointed cones to symbolize the active Mount Etna volcano.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Catanian chefs shape them like volcanic peaks, with red meat ragu inside mimicking the hot magma chamber.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: In Palermo, locals call them feminine 'arancine', while in Catania they fiercely insist on masculine 'arancini'.

facts_and_myths.claim: Arancini were created in Renaissance Venice using leftover risotto.
facts_and_myths.explanation: They originated in 10th-century Arab-ruled Sicily, combining saffron rice with meat fillings, later breaded for portability during hunting trips.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Sicily celebrates Saint Lucy's Day on December 13th by eating thousands of arancini instead of bread or pasta.

name: Tapas
visual_anchor: Bustling tavern bar counter filled with small earthenware dishes of garlic shrimp (gambas al ajillo), patatas bravas with spicy red sauce, and Spanish tortilla squares.
core_traits: Quintessential Spanish culinary culture of varied small savory appetizer dishes
Served in bars and taverns across Spain to accompany beer, vermouth, or wine
Staples include patatas bravas, gambas al ajillo, jamon iberico, and tortilla espanola
Eaten while bar-hopping on foot with friends, a social ritual called 'tapear'

facts_and_myths.claim: The word 'tapa' translates to 'lid' or 'cover', originally used to cover drink glasses.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Tavern keepers placed a slice of bread or ham over sherry glasses as a lid ('tapa') to keep out dust and flies, eventually adding toppings.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: In parts of Granada and Leon, bars still serve a complimentary free tapa with every drink ordered.

facts_and_myths.claim: Tapas are intended to be eaten seated at a formal banquet table with full silverware.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Tapas culture is famously casual and lively; diners stand around crowded bar counters, using toothpicks, fingers, and small napkins dropped on the floor.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: In the Basque country of northern Spain, tapas spiked onto bread with wooden toothpicks are called 'pintxos'.

name: Croquette
visual_anchor: Cylinder of golden, crispy deep-fried breadcrumbs broken open to show molten, silky bechamel sauce filled with bits of savory Spanish cured ham.
core_traits: Crisp, breadcrumbed deep-fried cylindrical roll with a creamy savory center
Spanish croquetas are made with thick, rich bechamel roux rather than mashed potatoes
Common fillings include cured Serrano ham (jamon), shredded chicken, or salt cod (bacalao)
French invention that spread across Europe, Latin America, and Japan (korokke)

facts_and_myths.claim: The name 'croquette' comes from the French verb 'croquer', meaning 'to crunch'.
facts_and_myths.explanation: It refers to the satisfying, audible shatter of the crispy breadcrumb crust when bitten into.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: In Japan, mashed-potato croquettes called 'korokke' are one of the most beloved supermarket deli comfort foods.

facts_and_myths.claim: Authentic Spanish bar croquetas are made by mashing boiled potatoes with cream.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Spanish croquetas use zero potato; the creamy interior is pure, slow-cooked bechamel sauce (butter, flour, milk) folded with minced ham or chicken.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Chilling the cooked bechamel dough overnight is required so it becomes firm enough to shape and bread.

name: Pasty
visual_anchor: Baked golden shortcrust pastry turnover with a thick, rope-crimped side crust, sliced open to reveal diced beef skirt, yellow swede turnip, potato, and onion.
core_traits: Traditional baked savory pastry turnover originating in Cornwall, southwest England
Historically carried by Cornish tin miners underground for midday sustenance
Filled with raw diced beef, sliced potato, yellow turnip (swede), and onion
Sealed with a thick, sturdy fluted rope crimp along the curved edge

facts_and_myths.claim: Cornish tin miners held the thick braided pastry crimp as a handle and discarded it to avoid arsenic poisoning.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Miners' hands were covered in toxic arsenic and copper dust; holding the crust allowed them to eat the pasty and throw away the contaminated handle.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Cornish Pasties have Protected Geographical Indication (PGI) status in the European Union and UK.

facts_and_myths.claim: Traditional Cornish pasty fillings are cooked in a skillet before being spooned into the dough.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Fillings must be placed into the raw pastry completely uncooked; they steam slowly in their own juices inside the sealed crust during baking.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Folklore says miners left the discarded crust corners to appease mischievous mine spirits called 'Knockers'.

name: Scotch Egg
visual_anchor: Deep-fried golden breadcrumb-crusted meat orb sliced cleanly in half, revealing a whole soft-boiled egg with jammy orange yolk wrapped in spiced sausage meat.
core_traits: British pub and picnic favorite consisting of a whole boiled egg wrapped in seasoned sausage meat
Coated in flour, beaten egg, and crisp breadcrumbs before being deep-fried or baked
Served hot with a runny jammy yolk in gastropubs, or cold at outdoor picnics
Accompanied by English whole-grain mustard or brown pickle relish

facts_and_myths.claim: London luxury department store Fortnum and Mason claims to have invented the Scotch Egg in 1738.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Fortnum and Mason created it as a portable, durable travel food for wealthy carriage passengers traveling to the countryside.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Despite the name, the dish has no verified origin in Scotland.

facts_and_myths.claim: Traditional Scotch eggs must always have chalky, gray-rimmed hard-boiled yolks.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Modern culinary standards prize soft-boiled eggs with velvety, jammy golden yolks that ooze slightly when cut.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: The dish may have been inspired by Indian Nargisi Kofta, hard-boiled eggs enclosed in spiced minced lamb.

name: Sausage Roll
visual_anchor: Golden, flaky puff pastry log with diagonal scored slits, filled with seasoned minced pork sausage, sliced into portions on a bakery rack.
core_traits: Popular British, Australian, and Commonwealth bakery and street snack
Seasoned minced pork sausage meat wrapped inside sheets of flaky puff pastry
Brushed with egg wash and baked in the oven until pastry is golden and puffed
Found in almost every high-street bakery, tea room, and sports stadium

facts_and_myths.claim: British bakery chain Greggs sells hundreds of millions of sausage rolls every single year.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Greggs is famous for selling roughly 2.5 million sausage rolls weekly, representing a massive cultural fast-food phenomenon.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Meat wrapped in pastry became wildly popular in 19th-century London as cheap street food.

facts_and_myths.claim: Sausage rolls are made with pre-cooked linked sausages with skins intact.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Sausage rolls use raw seasoned minced sausage meat without casing, which bonds smoothly to the pastry as it bakes.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: In Australia, sausage rolls are almost universally eaten squirted with cold tomato sauce (ketchup).

name: BLT Sandwich
